questions.question: State two factors that increase friction and two ways to reduce it.
questions.expected_answer: Increase: rougher surfaces; pressing the surfaces together harder (heavier object). Reduce: lubrication with oil or grease; using wheels, rollers or ball bearings; smoother surfaces; streamlining. Any two of each.

questions.question: Give one example where friction is useful and one where it is a nuisance, and explain each.
questions.expected_answer: Useful: brakes or tyre treads grip so vehicles can stop or walking is possible. Nuisance: engine parts or tyres wear away and energy is wasted as heat.

questions.question: Explain the difference between tension and compression, with an example of each.
questions.expected_answer: Tension is a pulling force along a stretched object such as a rope, cable or bridge cable. Compression is a squashing force along an object pressed from both ends, such as a table leg or a building pillar.
